div.head: Career Summary
div.p: Christian Lahusen was born in Argentina, son of Bremen merchant Heinrich Lahusen. He moved to Germany aged 13. He studied at the Leipzig Comservatory, and Leipzig University, and also as a private pupil of Hugo Riemann. In 1914 he was a repetiteur at the Charlottenburger Opera House. He served as a pilot in World War I. In 1919 he married Rahel Herrmann, who was Jewish. He worked as conductor and composer of the Munich Kammerspielen, and after 1920 also of the Hamburg Kammerspielen and the Frankfurt Playhouse. In 1924 he moved to Berlin and in 1930 to Überlingen on Lake Constance, where he remained for the rest of his life. Before 1930 he composed two ballets and four operas; after 1930 he composed mostly vocal music: religious and secular choral works and solo songs.

div.head: Lahusen and Schenker
div.p: Lahusen first visited Schenker unannounced on January 21, 1924, declaring himself a keen follower of Schenker’s writings. In May 1931, Lahusen wrote to Schenker professing to be a student of his and proclaiming that he had eschewed composition for five years and was studying strict counterpoint; in response, Schenker ordered a copy of Meisterwerk III to be sent to him. Little correspondence then ensued, but Schenker had a copy of his Fünf Urlinie-Tafeln sent to Lahusen in July 1932.

div.head: Correspondence
div.p: Four letters from Lahusen dating from 1931–32 are preserved as OJ 12/30, [1]–[4] and a clipping from the Frankfurter Zeitung concerning Lahusen’s Pantomime dated January 29, 1926 as OC C/279.
